method: 72 h 2-D back-trajectories from each state capital (arrivals 00/06/12/18 UTC daily), stepped hourly through ERA5 100 m winds; VIIRS hotspots within 25 km and ±3 h of the path counted once per trajectory, weighted by fire radiative power (FRP); hotspots assigned to Indonesian provinces by point-in-polygon.
wind_level: 100 m above ground (ERA5 via Open-Meteo archive; no 850 hPa in the archive)

params.national_weighting: Matched FRP summed over all 16 states, each state equal (the file also holds the plain mean of the 16 state shares)

data_sources.name: NASA FIRMS VIIRS S-NPP 375 m active fires, 2019 country archives (Indonesia, Malaysia, Brunei)
data_sources.licence: NASA open data (no restrictions; cite FIRMS)

data_sources.name: Open-Meteo Historical Weather API (ERA5 reanalysis), hourly 100 m wind
geoBoundaries gbOpen IDN ADM1 (Indonesian provinces, 2017; OSM/Wambacher) and ADM0 outlines

caveats: Single-level 2-D trajectories at 100 m: no vertical motion, dispersion, deposition or chemistry.
Wind sampled on a 1° grid and interpolated; paths over ~1,000 km carry growing position error.
Shares are of fire intensity (FRP) the air passed near, not measured smoke mass or PM2.5.
VIIRS sees fires only at ~01:30 and ~13:30 local overpasses; cloud and thick smoke hide fires; peat smoulders with low FRP.
One trajectory per state capital; a state is larger than one point.
Fires outside Indonesia, Malaysia and Brunei are not counted.
Provinces only; no companies or concessions are identified.
